A Weekend With No One in It

For the long, quiet weekend when nobody has called and the hours stretch out. It works on the two halves separately: making the time bearable now, and putting one thread out so next weekend has something in it.

Loneliness · Loneliness · Relationships · 8 items · whenever you need it

The checklist

  • Say it is loneliness, not a verdict — An empty weekend is a gap in the calendar, not proof about you.
  • Get out among people once — A coffee shop, a library, a store; being near others counts even without talking.
  • Send one message you would normally not send — “Thinking of you, how are things?” is enough to start.
  • Put a shape on the day — One thing in the morning and one in the afternoon; empty hours get heavier.
  • Move for twenty minutes — A walk changes the day more than another hour of scrolling will.
  • Notice who you scroll past — Watching other people’s weekends is not the same as having one.
  • Do one thing you would do for a guest — Cook properly, open the window, put music on; you count as company.
  • Put one thing on the calendar for next week — A class, a call, a coffee; loneliness eases through plans, not willpower.

Use this checklist Free account: tick items off and keep each day's record.

How to use it

Run through it whenever you need it, honestly and without scoring yourself. A checklist is a way of noticing, not a test: an item you cannot tick is information about the day, not a verdict on you. Over a few weeks the pattern of what gets ticked and what does not says more than any single pass.

With a free Theraglee account the checklist remembers each pass, so you can look back. Without one, you can still read it here and keep your own copy.
